exposure: Psychiatric comorbidity (depression, anxiety, new-onset depression/anxiety during pregnancy, prior depression/anxiety)
Nicotine, cannabis, and/or illicit substance use during and prior to pregnancy
cohort: The study included 789 pregnant women who tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 (asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic) and received care at Mayo Health System between March 2020 and October 2021.
finding: The study found that the prevalence rates of depression, anxiety, and prescribed antidepressant medications during pregnancy were substantially higher among asymptomatic and mildly symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infected women, which negatively impacted pregnancy and neonatal outcomes, including a significantly higher risk for cesarean delivery in those with psychiatric comorbidity.
mod_finding: Asymptomatic and mildly symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 positive pregnant women with psychiatric comorbidity had a significantly higher risk for cesarean delivery (35.6% vs. 24.9%).
